keyframe_review.note: 1420-1434: the Hussite union of Prague, Tábor and southern Bohemia, Hradec Králové/East Bohemia and Žatec-Louny; Plzeň, where Žižka 'could not hold it', became 'the major power of the Bohemian loyalists' (Landfrieden of Plzeň). Moravia was invaded but the Hussites 'returned to Bohemia'. The Taborites' campaigns reached Prachatice, Vodňany, Lomnice, Dvůr Králové, Polička, Vysoké Mýto and Chomutov (Taborites page). No area is given by either page.

correction.text: Tábor and the south Bohemian land of the Taborites (Sezimovo Ústí, Prachatice, Vodňany)

keyframe_review.note: After Lipany (30 May 1434) 'the power of the Taborites was broken' and 'the Sirotci union then disappeared'; in August 1435 the Taborites lost several castles at Křeč and a moderate wing took over. What remains is Tábor and the south, until the agreement of 25 January 1437.

region.text: Prague, the stronghold of the Praguers (Utraquists)

ledger.note: 30 July 1419: the first Defenestration of Prague opens the Hussite Wars (infobox 'Start: 30 July 1419'); Prague is the stronghold of the moderate Praguers (Utraquists). Sigismund, who claimed the crown, is not accepted.

region.text: Tábor and the south Bohemian land of the Taborites (Sezimovo Ústí, Prachatice, Vodňany)

ledger.note: Spring 1420: Tábor is founded. 'In the spring of 1420, a group of Hussites led by Petr Hromádka managed to seize the town of Sezimovo Ústí'; the Taborites are centred on Tábor in South Bohemia.

region.text: Hradec Králové and East Bohemia (the Orebite union)

ledger.note: East Bohemia joins the Hussites. The page gives no year: Hradec Králové was 'Under Utraquist rule, then adopted Tábor doctrine and called Žižka in', and East Bohemia was an Orebite union (renamed Orphans after 1424). Placed in 1420 as a bridge.

ledger.note: 1420: the first fighting. Žižka 'defeated Catholics at Sudoměř (25 March 1420)'; Pope Martin V's bull of 17 March 1420 proclaims a crusade; Sigismund arrives before Prague on 30 June and is defeated at Vítkov Hill (July) and Pankrác (1 November).

region.text: Žatec and Louny, the Hussite union of northern Bohemia

ledger.note: 1421: northern Bohemia is Hussite. 'Crusaders besieged Žatec in August 1421 and retreated': the Žatec-Louny union held by then.

region.text: the Hussite lands outside Tábor and the south

ledger.note: 30 May 1434: Lipany. The Taborite army 'was totally defeated and almost annihilated at the Battle of Lipany'; 'the power of the Taborites was broken'. The land outside Tábor and the south returns to the Utraquist-Catholic alliance and, with the Compacts of Jihlava (5 July 1436), to King Sigismund. The page does not list the places lost; the region is the 1420 shape without the Tábor land.

region.text: Tábor and the south Bohemian land of the Taborites (Sezimovo Ústí, Prachatice, Vodňany)

ledger.note: 25 January 1437: 'by mutual agreement with Sigismund, Tábor was promoted to royal town'. The Compacts had been 'formally accepted and signed at' Jihlava on 5 July 1436 (Hussite Wars page). The Taborites page ends the union's independent political power on 1 September 1452, when George of Poděbrady occupied Tábor.

region.text: Tábor and the south Bohemian land of the Taborites (Sezimovo Ústí, Prachatice, Vodňany)

ledger.note: 25 January 1437: Tábor becomes a royal town of King Sigismund's Bohemia.

ledger.note: January 1437: the Hussite state ends with Tábor's agreement with Sigismund; the Utraquist church continues inside the Kingdom of Bohemia under the Compacts.

wars.name: Hussite Wars

minus.text: Plzeň, the loyalist stronghold of the Landfrieden

zones.text: Bohemia without the loyalist stronghold of Plzeň: Prague, Tábor and the south, East Bohemia, Žatec-Louny

wars.outcome: Five crusades (1420, 1421, 1422, 1427, 1431) failed; Žižka's and Prokop's armies raided Silesia, Saxony, Lusatia, Hungary and Meissen; the Taborite army was annihilated at Lipany on 30 May 1434; the Compacts were signed at Jihlava on 5 July 1436.
wars.note: The page says the wars lasted 'from 1419 to approximately 1434' (infobox end 30 May 1434); 1436 is the Compacts. Dated raids: 1428 (Silesia, indirectly), 1433 (Neumark and Danzig, in the Polish-Teutonic War).

certainty.note: No page draws the Hussite lands as a boundary; the unions were held by towns and castles ('Landfrieden of Plzeň' for the loyalists), so the frontiers are approximate.

notes:
Hussite Bohemia is a rebel state Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-g flagged it with 'type rebel'). Its hatched colour sits inside the Kingdom of Bohemia's shape; the kingdom-of-bohemia dossier lists the Hussite Wars (1419-1434) but books no loss to the Hussites, so a gap-filler should add the matching loss events (1419, 1420, 1421) and gains (1434, 1437). Ends 1437-01, the last holdout's agreement; the Utraquist majority is treated as back in the kingdom after the Compacts of 1436.

Not settled: (1) The year East Bohemia (Hradec Králové) joined is on neither page (confidence 1). (2) The region lost in 1434 is a reading, the pages list no town. (3) The Hussite raids ('Spanilé jízdy') into Silesia, Lusatia, Saxony, Meissen and Hungary are undated on the pages (1428 and 1433 excepted); no occupation is booked. (4) The Hussite Wars page says the Polish Hussite movement ended at Grotniki in 1439; not drawn. (5) Moravia was invaded and not held. (6) The Taborites page dates the end of the union's independent power to 1 September 1452; this dossier closes at the January 1437 agreement. (7) No area on either page.
